cards.lore: You bend, you gather, you repeat.
cards.power: Keeps the player alive for one more turn.

cards.lore: The boy who won't sit still is sent out with the hounds.
cards.power: Distributes action points based on natural stats.

cards.lore: No one tracks who did how much; the day ends when there is enough.
cards.power: Ends the turn when the resource pool is full.

cards.lore: You no longer bend because you are hungry; you bend because you are the bender.
cards.power: Detaches production from appetite, creating infinite output.

cards.lore: The day has owners, and the owners are calling.
cards.power: Forces all units to pray in synchrony.

cards.lore: The factory's breath commands the herd.
cards.power: Converts time from something you pass into currency you spend.

cards.lore: Fourteen hours of the sun, all belonging to the mill.
cards.power: Treats daylight as the only legitimate constraint on availability.

cards.lore: The fiercest battle of the 19th century was over the right to go to sleep.
cards.power: Reclaims 8 hours of what we will from the opponent.

cards.lore: He timed every breath until Schmidt moved 47 tons.
cards.power: Breaks any job into terrifyingly efficient micro-motions.

cards.lore: The first manual for treating flesh like gears.
cards.power: Multiplies physical output by 400%; destroys the soul stat.

cards.lore: No one here knows how to make a pin.
cards.power: Multiplies output by 240; removes the ability to craft.

cards.lore: The structural prerequisite for mass amnesia.
cards.power: Prevents any worker from seeing the whole object.

cards.lore: The factory cannot function if the worker takes home what they make.
cards.power: Extracts all value beyond the bare minimum required for survival.

cards.lore: You build the world, but you do not live in it.
cards.power: The more wealth the worker produces, the poorer they become.

cards.lore: The Puritan wanted to work in a calling; we are forced to do so.
cards.power: Traps all participants; leaving requires ceasing to be modern.

cards.lore: In selling the hour, you sell the self that fills it.
cards.power: Turns human activity inside a community into a commodity for sale.

cards.lore: Invented to give you room; used to fence you in.
cards.power: Turns liberation into monolithic insanity.

cards.lore: The worker owns the means of production—their mind.
cards.power: Cannot be coerced; must be manipulated and persuaded.

cards.lore: The soft power of the new regime.
cards.power: Replaces the factory whistle with ambient dread.

cards.lore: The assembly bell of the white-collar world.
cards.power: Stops all actual work while simulating productivity.

cards.lore: The project takes six weeks because six weeks were allotted.
cards.power: Work automatically expands to fill allotted time.

cards.lore: The business shapes itself to what the analyst can see.
cards.power: Warps reality so the business only exists in three-month chunks.

cards.lore: The system now serves the measurement of the system.
cards.power: Overtakes the real value it was meant to represent.

cards.lore: Door-to-doctor time improved. The patient died.
cards.power: Once a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.

cards.lore: The real flows are sideways, informal, and invisible to the chartmakers.
cards.power: Tells a fiction about how decisions flow.

cards.lore: A periodic ritual where everyone pretends things have changed.
cards.power: Scrambles the chart while ignoring the underlying flow.

cards.lore: The place where the organization meets you once a year and pretends to know you.
cards.power: Generates mutual dishonesty.

cards.lore: The line was drawn before anyone looked at your work.
cards.power: Pre-determines the value of units before they are even considered.

cards.lore: A person writes the report no one will read.
cards.power: Allows the organization to claim it is doing something it isn't.

cards.lore: Re-entering data the machine lost.
cards.power: Exists solely to fix problems the platform refuses to repair.

cards.lore: Creating busywork for the capable.
cards.power: Manages units that absolutely do not require management.

cards.lore: Feudal retinues in cubicle clothing.
cards.power: Exists solely to make a superior feel important.

cards.lore: An arms race of useless aggression.
cards.power: Exists entirely because the opponent has one too.

cards.lore: The modern firm's imitation of the apprentice, journeyman, and master.
cards.power: Translates medieval guild progression into modern seniority.

cards.lore: You ask them who they are, and they answer what they do.
cards.power: The badge and the ceremony that bind the unit to the firm.

cards.lore: The exploiter is at the same time the exploited.
cards.power: Exploits itself, removing the need for a boss.

cards.lore: You have no one to blame, because the only one pushing was you.
cards.power: Triggers when the Achievement-Subject cannot stop being themselves.

cards.lore: Rediscovering work that pushes back.
cards.power: Answers you in a way the spreadsheet never will.

cards.lore: The whole object you can no longer build.
cards.power: Remembers what to do when the mind has been trained out of it.

cards.lore: Cannot survive the modern firm's hatred of slowness and mastery.
cards.power: Cares about doing the work well for its own sake.

cards.lore: The apprentice no longer apprentices. The apprentice is onboarded.
cards.power: Replaces deep mentorship with a PDF manual.

cards.lore: Labeled a crime by those who gave their souls for free.
cards.power: Refuses to give the firm more than it pays for.

cards.lore: Only by lying flat can humans be the measure of all things.
cards.power: Do nothing, achieve nothing, want nothing the system wants you to want.

cards.lore: Once a hobby; now a lifeboat.
cards.power: The only place where work that matters happens at all.

cards.lore: We got the productivity. We didn't get the time.
cards.power: A 1930s prophecy that raises productivity but deletes free time.

cards.lore: The structural unit of the new workday.
cards.power: Work that does not begin, because it has not ended.

cards.lore: Someone needed to clear their queue before logging off.
cards.power: Pierces time zones, the kitchen, the train, and the toilet.

cards.lore: A costume the office didn't know it was getting.
cards.power: Merges the bed and the desk into a single terrifying location.

cards.lore: Your job exists because no one has built a machine to do it yet.
cards.power: Does not need a quarterly. Can wait forever.

cards.lore: Surpassed by our own products.
cards.power: Induces shame at our own slowness.

cards.lore: Leisure planned around work, ended by work.
cards.power: A recovery period engineered to return you to work in better shape.

cards.lore: The activity for which work freed you. We have very little left.
cards.power: The activity that has no purpose outside itself.

cards.lore: The day did not have to be filled.
cards.power: A quantity of human time and attention.

cards.lore: After enough repetition, the other ways became unimaginable.
cards.power: The answer to the day. The way things are.

cards.lore: The morning is easier when the Job and the Calling are the same.
cards.power: What you do because you are the kind of being you are.

cards.lore: The system doesn't need us to know what it is for. But we need to know.
cards.power: The point of it all.

title: Bullshit Jobs Uncut: A Field Report from Before the Timesheet
